seed: Objects of type `marker` under action ACTION6 with touching neighbours [hazard,hit,wall] show mixed outcomes: gone x1, x,y x1. Find the condition in the before state that decides the outcome. Start from this kind of condition: the presence, type or relative position of a neighbouring object. Verify it against every transition before you keep it.

synth.notes:
Maze read from frame: floor colour 5, any other colour blocks; a 4x4 block/marker cell moves only if its destination is all floor (its own cells excepted).
Blocks 10 (armed 1): A1/A2 move both up/down 4, A3 moves them apart (left -4, right +4), A4 together; each block moves on its own.
Clicking colour 9 arms or switches (blocks->1, marker->11, old active->9); clicking colour 1 disarms; anything else, A5 and a click on the active marker are no-ops.
In armed mode A1-A4 move the active marker cell. HUD 0-bars on row 0 (right-aligned) and row 63 (left-aligned), w=3(a+1)//7; a carried over only while frames match, fallback = largest a for that width.
Hypothesis: the marker A6 gone vs x,y split is just objects being re-ranked and renamed on arm/switch, so it has no effect on the frame. Unconfirmed: what happens when two blocks aim for the same cell.
